correctness.rationale: Under the stated deterministic model, positive initial prevalence i, and unit recovery, infectious prevalence stays positive at finite times by its scalar linear equation with the current susceptible weights as coefficients. For cumulative pressure A, the susceptible classes are s p_j exp(−λ_j A) and recovered mass is A/R, so I=H_R(A)=1−sG(A)−A/R and A′=RI. H_R′(u)=s∑p_j λ_j exp(−λ_j u)−1/R is strictly decreasing, with exactly one root A_R under the given threshold. Because H_R≥i from 0 to A_R, the trajectory reaches the root in finite time, and strict increase of A gives a unique strict prevalence maximum. Factoring the root equation by its slowest decaying positive-class term yields A_R=log(R s p_*λ_*)/λ_*+o(1). In the time integral for R t_peak, replacing H_R by H_0 changes the integral by at most A_R²/(2Ri²)=o(1). The difference 1/H_0−1/(1−sp_0) is nonnegative and exponentially integrable, proving the constant and its sign. An independent endpoint check for a single positive class gives C=log((1−sp_0)/i)/(λ_*(1−sp_0)) by elementary substitution. The two-atom coefficients at a=1/2,1,0 are respectively 2,1,1/(2−s), giving eventual strict ordering. At fixed R in the supercritical regime the root varies continuously with a by strict monotonicity and joint continuity, and the integral has denominator bounded below by i; hence the maximum is attained in the interior at sufficiently large fixed R and the iterated normalized limits differ. Coalescence at a=1 doubles p_* relative to the noncoalesced case, and at a=0 the zero-rate term drops out of the derivative, as required.
residual_risks: The numerical check solves the same pressure equations for selected parameters; it is not independent evidence of the all-law asymptotic. The proof is for fixed s and fixed finite F, not uniform near a=0; no claim about incidence peaks, final size or stochastic finite-population timing is verified by this argument.

value.rationale: Peak time is an observable not determined just by the reproduction threshold or final size. The fixed-law expansion shows that, unlike the common mean susceptibility, the slowest positive class and exactly immune mass set the leading timing coefficient. The explicit finite offset gives precision beyond the logarithmic rate. The mean-preserving example exhibits a strict interior-later ordering and a noncommuting limit even though, at fixed transmission, the timing is continuous in mixture parameter. This is a useful structural distinction in the stated mathematical model, not a calibrated prediction.
residual_risks: No uniform transition asymptotic, finite-population theorem, incidence-peak law, or real-world parameter prescription is claimed.
